narrative_markdown:
## Overview
Warm and sunny today, much like yesterday. With convective instability rising significantly in evening models, isolated thunder is possible tonight, peaking around 20:00 local time, though models disagree sharply on convective strength.

## Today's Forecast
The morning starts with sunny intervals as temperatures quickly rise from dawn lows near 19°C / 66°F to an afternoon high around 31°C / 88°F. Winds will pick up from the southwest by afternoon, reaching 20–25 km/h (11–13 kt) with gusts up to 37 km/h (20 kt). Peak UV index will reach 9.2 around midday, requiring sun protection. Although measurable rainfall is not expected today—a call shared across all numerical models and the Kenya Meteorological Department—convective instability surges after dusk. UKMO and ICON project CAPE building to 1100–1430 J/kg between 19:00 and 22:00, creating potential for nocturnal thunder despite dry surface projections, while GFS and ECMWF show much lower instability (<300 J/kg). Nighttime lows will settle near 18°C / 64°F under partly cloudy skies. Air quality assessment relies on CAMS model data as all local ground sensors are currently stale; CAMS predictions show moderate US AQI levels peaking near 86.

## Extended Outlook
Days 1–3 (Friday to Sunday) will remain warm and predominantly dry across Nyanza Basin, with daytime highs ranging between 32°C / 90°F and 34°C / 93°F and overnight lows around 19°C–20°C (66°F–68°F). Afternoon southwesterly winds will remain brisk, with peak gusts reaching 35–45 km/h (19–24 kt). Looking out to Days 4–7 (Monday through Thursday), precipitation probabilities increase by Monday and Tuesday as atmospheric moisture returns to the basin, with ECMWF and ICON indicating scattered afternoon and evening showers (1–4 mm total) and a slight drop in daytime highs back toward 30°C / 86°F.

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential
No widespread severe weather or heavy rainfall hazards are anticipated during daylight hours. However, elevated convective instability (CAPE exceeding 1400 J/kg on UKMO and 1100 J/kg on ICON) develops after dusk, peaking around 20:00. While measurable surface rain accumulation is not expected, lightning hazards and localized convective wind gusts remain a secondary possibility overnight.

## Lake Victoria — Conditions for Boaters
Offshore conditions over open waters will see moderate southwesterly winds developing by mid-afternoon at 12–18 km/h (6–10 kt) with gusts to 23 km/h (12 kt), producing light chop. Overnight, boater vigilance is strongly advised: instability over the lake surges dramatically, with UKMO projecting extreme CAPE values above 2500–3100 J/kg and ECMWF above 1800–2100 J/kg between midnight and dawn. This supports nighttime convective development over open water, bringing risks of sudden thunderstorm squalls, erratic wind shifts, and localized rough lake conditions despite dry shore forecasts.

## Detailed Discussion
### Synoptic Overview
Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the northeast (1004 hPa) and highest toward the southeast (1017 hPa) — a 14 hPa spread, a strong large-scale gradient. Pressure is also falling toward the north, northwest, and south — a large-scale feature building in that direction, though this sampling cannot say how fast or whether it will reach here. Pressure overhead is falling, with mean MSLP dropping roughly 1.3 hPa over 24 hours to 1012.4 hPa. Across the Nyanza Basin sub-points, mean surface pressure ranges from 1012.4 hPa at Kisumu to 1014.8 hPa at Kisii, maintaining a typical weak basin gradient during the day before nocturnal lake-breeze convergence develops.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes
At Day+0, Best Match (87% all-time rain accuracy) and ECMWF (90% rolling 10-check) lead rain accuracy rankings. The Kenya Meteorological Department (KMD) bulletin calls for sunny intervals during the day and partly cloudy conditions tonight with a maximum of 32.0°C / 90°F and minimum of 17.0°C / 63°F, aligning closely with numerical consensus for a dry day. Confidence in dry surface conditions is high given universal model agreement on <0.6 mm rainfall. However, confidence regarding nighttime convection is moderate due to a prominent CAPE divergence: UKMO (1430 J/kg) and ICON (1130 J/kg) indicate significant nocturnal instability, whereas GFS (100 J/kg) remains largely stable. As noted in historical verification notes from similar synoptic setups (e.g. August 28 and 30), elevated nighttime CAPE frequently yields lightning without measurable surface rainfall. Additionally, long-run review findings show GFS systematically under-forecasts peak wind (mean error +21.2 km/h at Day+0), so peak wind gusts are weighted toward ECMWF/ICON guidance (~37 km/h).

Ground AQI sensors at Kisumu Airport (AQI 13), Ochieng' Avenue (AQI 43), and Dunga Beach (AQI 32) last reported 3 hours ago and are flagged as stale; the last known ground reading was AQI 43 at Ochieng' Avenue. Therefore, live air quality relies on CAMS reanalysis.
